newsitem.title: USA: Ryerson Tull closes Thypin Steel purchase.
newsitem.headline: Ryerson Tull closes Thypin Steel purchase.

text.p: Ryerson Tull Inc said Friday it has completed a previously announced acquisition of Thypin Steel Co Inc, a privately held distributor and processor of carbon and stainless steel products, for $120 million in cash.
In addition, Ryerson Tull assumed $23 million in existing Thypin debt.

"We believe the metals service center industry is in the early stages of consolidation, and we expect to be an active participant in that process," said Neil Novich, president and chief executive officer of Ryerson Tull, in a statement.
He said the acquisition of Thypin significantly increases Ryerson Tull's presence in the eastern United States.
Thypin has seven facilities, located in New York's Long Island City and Buffalo, N.Y.; Cambridge, Mass.; Easton and Fairless Hills, Pa.; Charlotte, N.C.; and Birmingham, Ala.
Ryerson Tull is North America's largest distributor and processor of metals and has annual revenues of about 2.7 billion. Inland Steel Industries Inc owns 87 percent of the stock of Ryerson Tull.
Shares of Ryerson Tull were trading unchanged at 15.
